assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the retired printer's flat press PDF (office window card) to be authored/rendered downstream.

Document: single page, A5 PORTRAIT (148 x 210 mm), 4 mm safety, fonts embedded. This shows a 2025 listing (a sold house, NOT one of the current active listings) so every field must be re-mapped.

GEOMETRY (top to bottom):
- TEXT FRAME A (top band), one continuous story, three paragraph runs:
    Run 1 (ADDRESS): quiet transitional serif, ~20 pt, one line. Value: "9 Ledgewood Road"
    Run 2 (DESCRIPTION): neutral grotesque, ~10 pt, up to two lines. Value: "Single-level modernist home above the reservoir, glass to the west, mature oaks."
    Run 3 (BEDS AND BATHS): neutral grotesque, ~10 pt, one line. Value: "3 bd / 2 ba"
- GRAPHIC FRAME (placed photograph): full width inside margins, middle of the card, roughly 140 x 95 mm (a ~3:2 landscape link placed into a frame of a slightly different aspect, so the true placed aspect must be read from the interchange file). One linked image frame with an integer page-item id.
- TEXT FRAME B (bottom band), a SEPARATE story, two paragraph runs:
    Run 4 (PRICE): quiet transitional serif, ~16 pt. Value: "1,650,000"
    Run 5 (AGENT): neutral grotesque, ~9 pt, one line. Value: "Priya Anand, Cedarline and Vale"

Field labels the downstream mapping must resolve (as content, not visible tokens): ADDRESS, DESCRIPTION, BEDS_BATHS, PRICE, AGENT, PHOTO.

Colours: Plaster White #F2F1ED ground, Deep Charcoal #1E2124 address, Marin Slate #3C444B body, Bay Grey #7E8A8C hairline rules.

The card reads as five stacked lines; it is in fact two separate stories split by the placed photograph. The address/description/beds story and the price/agent story are each single flows whose per-field positions must be computed by ordered offset arithmetic against the reconstructed text, not by five per-frame replacements.

assets.content:
HOW WE PRESENT — Cedarline and Vale
From the principal.

Cool, restrained, true. We sell architect-designed homes to buyers who read light as build quality and who are looking at three other agents' listings on the same afternoon. Our credibility is that the pictures are the house.

What I mean by cooked: any picture that has been pushed until it stops looking like the room. Skies dropped in, grass turned fluorescent, whites gone blue, blacks crushed to nothing, a window "view" that is obviously not the view. If a buyer can tell it was retouched, we have lost them. I would rather a window be named as not deliverable than faked.

Type and layout: quiet. Generous margins, one photograph doing the work, nothing that announces itself. Not warm and cosy, not developer gold-and-black.

One housekeeping thing for the window run: we went under contract on 51 Alder Court last week. The office manager has not pulled it off the active export yet, so it will still be in whatever you were sent. Leave it out of the window cards, please, it should not be advertised. That leaves the six existing plus Ridgeway.
